description: US Social Security for people born in 1960 or later (full retirement age 67): the monthly benefit at each claiming age from 62 to 70 from the full-retirement-age amount (5/9 of 1% a month for the first 36 months early, 5/12 of 1% beyond, so 62 = 70%; 2/3 of 1% a month delayed, so 70 = 124%; rounded down to the dollar as SSA does), lifetime totals to a chosen age in today’s dollars, and the break-even age between two claiming ages (62 vs 70 about 80.4, 62 vs 67 about 78.7, 67 vs 70 82.5). One person’s own benefit; no spousal or survivor benefits. Use this when someone asks when to claim Social Security, how much less it is at 62, or the break-even age.

monthlyAt67.description: Monthly benefit at full retirement age 67, USD (from the my Social Security statement)

toAge.description: Count lifetime benefits to this age (default 85)
